title: Ordinary integral module pullback and its strict quotient completion map
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation ring $R$ and a uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Set $B_W=\varprojlim_{n\geq0}(R/t^{n+1})_W$, with quotient projections $\pi_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. The constant-section maps $\rho_n:(R/t^{n+1})_Y\to f_*(R/t^{n+1})_X$ are those of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Define $\rho:B_Y\to f_*B_X$ by the limit equations $f_*(\pi_{X,n})\rho=\rho_n\pi_{Y,n}$, and let $c_f:f^{-1}B_Y\to B_X$ be its adjoint. Define the module direct image $f^B_*$ to be sectionwise direct image with action through $\rho$. Define its ordinary additive module left adjoint $f_B^*Q=B_X\otimes_{f^{-1}B_Y}f^{-1}Q$, with the sheafified module Kan-extension adjunction, using sheaves of modules and sheaf tensor product [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Apply $f_B^*$ termwise to cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For such a complex $Q$, let $Q_n=Q\otimes_{B_Y}(R/t^{n+1})_Y$ and let $K_n=\operatorname{Res}_n f_n^*Q_n$, with the strict quotient transitions and finite pullbacks used in the completed integral operations [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Define the quotient augmentation $a_n:f_B^*Q\to K_n$ on local tensor generators by $b\otimes q\mapsto1\otimes(q\otimes\pi_{X,n}(b))$. Its product $a:f_B^*Q\to\prod_n K_n$ is killed by $1-s$ for these actual transitions. Define the completion chain map $f_B^*Q\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ to have coordinates $(a,0)$, with the zero cochain in the shifted product; the target is the strict-tower derived-limit model [def-weil-derived-limit]. This defines the ring map, module functors, adjunction, termwise pullback, quotient augmentation and completion chain map; it makes no assertion that ordinary pullback preserves constructibility or that its completion comparison is invertible.

The result is the difference between the two sides of the quotient augmentation naturality square for n+1 to n, hence zero. Product projections are jointly monic. The differential of the zero second cochain is zero. This obligation is proved in Lean, conditional on the original quotient-augmentation existence theorem, whose proof remains pending.
